newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: The Spanish yield curve flattened on Tuesday, as the long end outperformed a short end dragged lower by uncertainty over EMU's future.

"People are selling the short end, while short coverings are pushing the long end higher," a dealer at one of the major Spanish banks said. "Good Spanish fundamentals are supporting the long end, while EMU uncertainty is taking its toll on the peseta and the short end," he added.
Dealers forecast that yields at Wednesday's auction of one-year and 18-month paper will pick up slightly, with the Bank of Spain expected to hold its key money rate steady for now.
On the long bond future, chartists pegged first resistance at 115.68, and then at 115.80. After Tuesday's performance, they said strong support lay at 115.00.
Markets were largely unaffected by comments from Montoro that a delay in the start of Europe's single currency was not politically viable, dealers said.
"Uncertainties are always there. Maybe after the Amsterdam summit, the underlying tone of the market will improve a bit," a dealer in Madrid said.
The EU Amsterdam summit will take place on June 16 and 17.
